mechanism_narrative: The sharp simultaneous collapse in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT will continue to depress discretionary trips, so retail and recreation mobility stays below its prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining at least 15 points below baseline for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls below -50 percent and WORKPLACES stays below -40 percent, a restriction-like regime is in force that suppresses shopping trips within one to two weeks and keeps RETAIL_REC down.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -50 and WORKPLACES falls below -40
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -70.9 and WORKPLACES at t-0w is -48.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior four-week mean in the two weeks after the threshold crossing, or it rebounds while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A steep rise in RESIDENTIAL time signals substitution toward staying home; if this persists, retail visits fall over the next four weeks because discretionary errands are replaced by at-home activity.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days when RESIDENTIAL remains above +10 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent drop in PARKS and RETAIL_REC after a prior positive PARKS reading indicates weather or seasonal suppression of outdoor activity; that same shock should keep retail recreation weak for the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from positive to below 0
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moves from 7.0 at t-1w to -51.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds within one week after PARKS turns negative and stays negative, with no corresponding improvement in other mobility series.

mechanism_narrative: The combined weakness in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates broad trip suppression rather than a category shift, so retail mobility should remain depressed over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean within two weeks while GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS stay below their t-1w levels.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid transit shock is the leading indicator: once TRANSIT drops more than 20 points week-on-week, retail and recreation declines further over the next four weeks as access constraints propagate into discretionary travel.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT falls from -38.3 at t-1w to -70.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: After a >20 point weekly drop in TRANSIT, RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM weakens together with WORKPLACES, the population is shifting into a broad caution mode that suppresses mixed-purpose outings and pulls RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -10 while WORKPLACES stays below -20
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is -26.7 and WORKPLACES is -48.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks after the joint threshold is met, or it rises while both proxies remain weak.

mechanism_narrative: In a commuting-collapse regime, low WORKPLACES mobility translates into fewer lunchtime and after-work shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC stays below its recent average for the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC moves above its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below -30 for at least two consecutive weeks.
